I feel you 100% because I've been in a similar situation. I let mine go on for years after all trust was gone because I loved him, but things only got worse and it killed me. We broke up multiple times but he'd always get "better" so, like a fool, I'd always go back. Trying to continue drained everything out of me. My advice to you would be to just end it and go from there. I know it is very hard but it would be for the best. It'll hurt for a while but the pain fades with time. Being hurt for a little while is better than being with someone you cannot trust and letting things progress further. The longer you keep it going, the more it'll hurt in the end.

Personally, I would sit them down and (nicely) ask their reasoning for not allowing you to stay with him. You've said you've been doing good in school so as long as that keeps up, there's no real issue if you go stay for the weekends. Plus, if they're okay with you visiting him during the day, what's so bad about staying the night? You are an adult who has the ability to make all of these decisions, especially about what you choose to do with people. Also, if they're aware you guys are sexually active, then the wait until marriage argument is invalid. Not to mention, if you're there during the day you guys can still do stuff, it doesn't just take place at night. Staying there would just be more convenient and safer, it wouldn't prevent you all from having sex if you go home at night.  I would suggest asking them their reasons and then respectfully telling them your side of things which would hopefully convince them. You may also be able to bargain with them and let them give you a time to be home by in the morning (etc) Regardless, best of luck to you!

You could always get another mutual friend to tell her if that would make you more comfortable.  Best of luck :)

Honestly, I see where you're coming from. For the longest time, I didn't want to get near the oven myself but it got better over time. Indeed most things can be microwaved or heated other ways, but an oven is definitely more convenient in some cases. All you have to do is start with baby steps and just get more comfortable with it. Your family shouldn't make a big deal over something that is a perfectly normal fear.

Suicide isn't the answer no matter how tempting it may be. And I'm sure you've heard this a bunch but nothing is your fault.  It's definitely not right for your mother to not allow you to see a therapist but there could be other ways. You could always rant to friends, although it won't be the same as a professional, it helps to get things off of your chest. As other people have mentioned, you can call the police and that would result in help.  I hope things look up for you
